content: 1. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Erythromycin stearate and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Concomitant use should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be considered. Panobinostat prescribing information advises against its use with drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. 3. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 4. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per dosage modification guidelines. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. 5. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. Erythromycin stearate and perphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per dosage modification guidelines. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases the effects of phenindione by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 9. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 10. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of pitavastatin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Additionally, erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of pitavastatin, potentially increasing the risk of myopathy due to OATP1B1 inhibition. 12. Erythromycin stearate and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 15. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while prednisone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 17. Erythromycin stearate and pretomanid both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid regimens are associated with hepatotoxicity, and alcohol or other hepatotoxic agents should be avoided. 18. Erythromycin stearate and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Erythromycin stearate and prochlorperazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Erythromycin stearate and promazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Erythromycin stearate and promethazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Erythromycin stearate increases the effects of protamine by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Erythromycin stearate and protriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 27. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels of erythromycin stearate by decreasing its metabolism, leading to a risk of prolonged QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 28. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 30. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 31. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by mechanisms involving OATP1B1/3 transport inhibition. Avoid coadministration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 32. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of revefenacin by mechanisms involving OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transport inhibition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 33. Ribociclib increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of rifabutin by decreasing its metabolism, while rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 35. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 36. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 37. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 38. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of riociguat by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 39. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while ritonavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 41. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 42. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous selumetinib dose. 43. Erythromycin stearate and sertraline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Erythromycin stearate and sevoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 46. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Additionally, siponimod and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. 47. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 48. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Additionally, solifenacin and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. 49. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 50. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 51. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam by mechanisms involving OATP1 transport inhibition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 52. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Additionally, sunitinib and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. 53. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Additionally, tacrolimus and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. 54. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. For daily use, limit tadalafil to 5 mg/day or 10 mg every 72 hours as needed. 55. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per dosage modification guidelines. 56. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 57. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 58. Erythromycin stearate and tetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 59. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 60. Erythromycin stearate and thioridazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 61. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 62. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 63. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 64. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 65. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 66. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of toremifene by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use is unavoidable, closely monitor the patient with ECGs for QT prolongation. 67. Erythromycin stearate and trazodone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 68. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while triamcinolone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 69. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 70. Erythromycin stearate and trifluoperazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 71. Erythromycin stearate and trimipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 72. Trofinetide increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by mechanisms involving OATP transport inhibition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 73. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 74. Erythromycin stearate decreases the effects of the live typhoid vaccine by pharmacodynamic interactions. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
